vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: review-evo
Version: 0.1.0

The skill's actions are fully aligned with its stated purpose as a 'self-improving code reviewer'. It primarily uses local `git` commands and file system operations (`ls`, `mkdir`, read/write to `.review-evo/learnings.md`) within the context of the repository. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized network activity, persistence mechanisms, or malicious prompt injection attempts against the agent. All file access and command executions are local and directly support the analysis of code and git history, with learnings stored locally as intended.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions match its stated purpose — it analyzes git history and persists a local knowledge file — but it will read the whole repository and create/append .review-evo/learnings.md in your project.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim a self-improving code reviewer based on git history; the SKILL.md only uses git commands, reads repository files, and writes a local .review-evo/learnings.md — all consistent with that purpose. No unrelated cloud credentials, services, or install actions are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions instruct the agent to run many git commands, read many files, and open files throughout the repository (including reading and creating .review-evo/learnings.md). This is expected for a repo-wide reviewer but means the agent will see any sensitive files present in the repository (secrets, credentials, config). The instructions also ask to read full files before summarizing and to scan commit history (last 50 commits, churn analysis, etc.).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — instruction-only skill, so nothing will be downloaded or written by an installer. The only declared required binary is git, which matches the commands. Minor note: the instructions also rely on common shell tools (ls, mkdir, awk, sort, head, awk fallback) but these are standard on Unix-like systems; they are not declared as required binaries.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no credentials, and no external config paths. That is proportionate to its stated function.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists a learnings file in the repository (.review-evo/learnings.md) and will create the .review-evo directory. It does not request 'always: true'. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default). Persisting to the repo is consistent with the described 'self-improving' behavior but is a persistent change to your project that you should be aware of and review.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its purpose, but be aware it will read your entire repository and write .review-evo/learnings.md into the project root. Before running: (1) avoid running it on repositories that contain secrets or private credentials; (2) review and commit/inspect the created .review-evo/learnings.md before sharing it externally; (3) if you run on Windows or a restricted shell, some awk/shell commands may fail — run in a POSIX-like environment or check the fallback behavior; (4) if you want no persistent artifacts, remove or ignore the .review-evo directory after the run. If you want extra assurance, run the git commands manually first to inspect outputs the skill would consume.
